paragraphs: R. Chiyya, son of Rabbah bar Nachmani, student of R. Yishmael the amora. In Sanhedrin 69b, beginning: “R. Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani said: Rav Chisda said”; some say, “Rav Chisda said: Zeiri said.” I think it should read “Rav Chisda said: Rav said; and some say, etc.” Berakhot 43a, near the end: “R. Chiyya son of Abba”—it should read Rabbah—“bar Nachmani said: Rav Chisda said: Rav said”; some say, “Rav Chisda said: Zeiri said.” Avodah Zarah 49b: “R. Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani said: R. Chisda said: Zeiri said: the law follows R. Eliezer.” Some say, “R. Chisda said: Abba bar Rav Chisda told me: thus Zeiri said, the law follows R. Eliezer.” There, 60b, near the end: “R. Chiyya son of Abba”—it should read Rabbah—“bar Nachmani said: R. Chisda said: Rav said”; some say, “R. Chisda said: Zeiri said: the law follows R. Shimon.” Some say, “R. Chisda said: Abba bar Chanan told me: thus Zeiri said, the law follows R. Shimon.” Yuchasin, letter alef, writes: “In chapter R. Yishmael: R. Chisda said: Abba bar Cham told me. Rav Tzemach Gaon bar Paltoya explains in his Arukh that this is a sage's name.” End of quotation. You will not find Abba bar Cham in chapter R. Yishmael, only what I have transcribed here. See for yourself that it is an error. Avodah Zarah 31a has “R. Chiyya son of R. Chiyya bar Nachmani said: R. Chisda said: Rav said”; some say, “R. Chisda said: Zeiri said”; and some say, “R. Chisda said: Abba bar Chama told me: thus Zeiri said, the law follows R. Eliezer.” Go and see: in my opinion, without doubt, “R. Chiyya son of R. Chiyya bar Nachmani said” should read “R. Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani said,” as in all the aforementioned places. Yuchasin erred in listing Rav Chiyya bar Chiyya, for he is not found anywhere in the Talmud except the place cited above, and I have already shown you that this is a scribal error. Yuchasin also listed Abba bar Rav Chisda, Abba bar Chanan, and Abba bar Chama, mentioned in those Avodah Zarah passages; they are mentioned nowhere else in the Talmud. You will also find in Rosh Hashanah 34b, near the end: Rabbah bar bar Chana said in R. Yochanan's name, “The sages agree with Rabban Gamliel.” Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani heard it—“Rabbi” [in the new Talmud editions]—and went and stated the teaching before Rav Dimi bar Chinena, who said, “Thus Rav said.” As for Yuchasin's statement that he was a student of R. Yishmael the amora: these are merely prophetic assertions, that he was a student of an amora named Rabbi Yishmael. Apparently this arose from Berakhot, chapter Sheloshah SheAkhelu, 48b, near the end: “R. Chiyya bar Nachmani, student of R. Yishmael, in R. Yishmael's name.” End of quotation. The author of Yuchasin saw R. Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani speaking in Rav Chisda's and R. Dimi bar Chinena's names, who lived many generations after R. Yishmael the tanna. How, then, could Berakhot say he was R. Yishmael's student? It supposedly followed necessarily that this R. Yishmael was an amora. See, however, that he erred in two respects. The statement in Sheloshah SheAkhelu, where R. Chiyya bar Nachmani speaks in R. Yishmael's name, is mentioned in Mekhilta, portion Bo, section 16. It is known that R. Yishmael, R. Akiva's colleague and a tanna, composed the Mekhilta. Moreover, both Sheloshah SheAkhelu and Mekhilta say R. Chiyya bar Nachmani, not “son of Rabbah bar Nachmani.” They are therefore not one person. The one in Mekhilta and Sheloshah SheAkhelu is the earlier R. Chiyya bar Nachmani, student of R. Yishmael the tanna; the one mentioned in Sanhedrin, Rosh Hashanah, and Avodah Zarah is R. Chiyya son of Rabbah bar Nachmani. He was neither the student of R. Yishmael the tanna nor the student of R. Yishmael an amora, for you will not find an unqualified “Rabbi Yishmael” among the amoraim. Examine this and you will find that he erred in four or five matters. The new Talmud editions likewise did not correct the three aforementioned places in Avodah Zarah where there must be scribal errors.
